Canvas_Ref.x-normalization: NONE; exact Unicode scalar sequence; never trim/lower/NFC; not a path

Canvas_CatalogueFacts.x-meaning: The world source material vocabulary with names, colours and the neutral orientation index. presentation has exactly the Catalogue materials as keys; orientationIndex describes every orientation any material declares.

Canvas_Catalogue.x-meaning: The world source's own material vocabulary. emptyMaterialRef names the material that means an empty cell; it must be a key of materials.

Canvas_EngineRevisions.x-meaning: Opaque revisions the world source reports for what defines its materials. Compared for equality only.

Canvas_Revision.x-normalization: NONE; opaque equality, never numeric ordering

Canvas_MaterialTags.x-meaning: Neutral tags the world source normalises from its own material definitions. placeable is the world source's conclusion that the material can be written and restored on its declared write path with no side effect and no persistent state; null is unknown and never treated as false or true. Raw engine fields stay in extension and are never read outside the world source.

Canvas_Orientation.x-meaning: Neutral orientation index of a material, from the set the Catalogue declares for that material. Conversion to an engine encoding happens only inside the world source.

Canvas_OpaqueValue.x-meaning: Any strict JSON value owned by the world source. Carried and digested unchanged; never interpreted outside the world source.

Canvas_MaterialPresentation.x-meaning: How the world source names and colours one material for people and for image material matching. null is unknown, never a default name or colour.

Canvas_SrgbColor.x-meaning: An sRGB colour as lower-case #rrggbb. The world source decides how it is obtained (declared, or from its own assets); consumers compare and match colours only.

Canvas_OrientationDescriptor.x-meaning: Neutral meaning of one orientation index: clockwise quarter turns about the Frame up axis seen from above, and whether the material is flipped upside down. null means the world source has no neutral expression for that part; the conversion to an engine encoding stays inside the world source.

World_Ref.x-normalization: NONE; exact Unicode scalar sequence; never trim/lower/NFC; not a path

World_MaterialSourceFacts.x-meaning: Material sources and colours for image material selection. presentation has exactly the materialRefs of snapshot.materials as keys. Texture bytes are not on the wire: they are referenced by bytesDigest and travel through the in-process material sources port.

World_EngineRevisions.x-meaning: Opaque revisions the world source reports for what defines its materials. Compared for equality only.

World_Revision.x-normalization: NONE; opaque equality, never numeric ordering

World_Orientation.x-meaning: Neutral orientation index of a material, from the set the Catalogue declares for that material. Conversion to an engine encoding happens only inside the world source.

World_MaterialPresentation.x-meaning: How the world source names and colours one material for people and for image material matching. null is unknown, never a default name or colour.

World_SrgbColor.x-meaning: An sRGB colour as lower-case #rrggbb. The world source decides how it is obtained (declared, or from its own assets); consumers compare and match colours only.

EngineRevisions.x-meaning: Opaque revisions the world source reports for what defines its materials. Compared for equality only.

Revision.x-normalization: NONE; opaque equality, never numeric ordering

Raw engine fields stay in extension and are never read outside the world source.

nativeErrorSemantics.default: DSH uses original Error.message or String(value), content text Error: <message>, isError true, error.message; HarnessError alone yields optional info {name,code}.
nativeErrorSemantics.identity: Plugin promise rejects original object; Tools normalized result is lossless JSON and does not preserve object identity, stack/cause/custom fields unless present in original message. No promise of false serialization identity.
nativeErrorSemantics.policy: Upstream normal hooks may replace/block outcomes; this tool adds no policy bypass or custom success/error wrapper
